headerLines: THIRD YEAR SECOND SEMESTER SUPPLEMENTARY EXAMINATION 2023
INTRODUCTION TO STATISTICAL AND PROBABILISTIC METHODS (HONS.)
parts.scriptNote: Use a separate Answer-Script for each part
parts.instructions: Answer any THREE questions. Two marks reserved for neatness and well organized answers.

rows.topic: Bayes' Theorem
rows.textLatex: A company uses three different assembly lines—$A_1$, $A_2$, and $A_3$—to manufacture a particular component. Of those manufactured by line $A_1$, $5\%$ need rework to remedy a defect, whereas $8\%$ of $A_2$'s components need rework and $10\%$ of $A_3$'s need rework. Suppose that $50\%$ of all components are produced by line $A_1$, $30\%$ are produced by line $A_2$, and $20\%$ come from line $A_3$. If a randomly selected component needs rework, what is the probability that it came from line $A_1$? From line $A_2$? From line $A_3$?

rows.topic: Properties of CDF & PDF (Discrete vs Continuous)
rows.textLatex:
Enlist the properties of probability distribution functions (pdf) of random variables. How can you distinguish the pdfs of discrete random variables from those of continuous random variables?
How can you derive the probability density function from the probability distribution function? Explain.

rows.topic: Normal Distribution & Linear Interpolation
rows.textLatex:
The breakdown voltage of a randomly chosen diode of a certain type is known to be normally distributed with mean value $40\text{ V}$ and standard deviation $1.5\text{ V}$. (i) What is the probability that the breakdown voltage of a single diode is between $39\text{ V}$ and $42\text{ V}$? (ii) What value is such that only $15\%$ of all diodes have breakdown voltages exceeding that value?
Use the attached table for standard Gaussian random variable. Perform linear interpolation if necessary.

rows.topic: Memoryless Property of Exponential Distribution
rows.textLatex: Prove the 'Lack-of Memory' property of exponential random variables. Explain the significance of this property.

rows.topic: Markov's and Chebyshev's Inequalities
rows.textLatex: Derive Markov's inequality and Chebyshev's inequality. Explain the significances of these bounds. Which one is a tighter bound and why?

rows.topic: Joint PDF, Joint CDF & Marginal Density
rows.textLatex:
Two random variables, $X$ and $Y$, have a joint probability density function given by
$$f(x, y) = Kxy \quad \text{for } 0 \le x \le 1 \; ; \; 0 \le y \le 1$$
$$= 0 \text{ elsewhere.}$$
(i) Determine the value of $K$ that makes this a valid probability density function.
(ii) Determine the joint probability distribution function $F(x, y)$.
(iii) Find the joint probability of the event $X \le \frac{1}{2}$ and $Y > \frac{1}{2}$.
(iv) Find the marginal density function $f(x)$.

rows.topic: Validity of Power Spectral Density Expressions
rows.textLatex:
If $X(t)$ is a real wide-sense stationary (WSS) random process, examine whether or not the following are valid expressions for power spectral density. Justify your answers.
(i) $S_X(\omega) = \dfrac{6}{6 + 7\omega^3}$
(ii) $S_X(\omega) = \dfrac{40}{4 + \omega^2}$

rows.topic: Cross-Correlation Bound for Jointly WSS Processes
rows.textLatex:
Justify or correct the following statement with suitable reasoning/ derivation
"Magnitude of cross-correlation of two jointly WSS random processes can never exceed the product of the rms values of the processes".

rows.topic: Ergodic Process
rows.textLatex: What is an Ergodic Process?

rows.topic: Gamma Distribution, PGF & WSS Autocorrelation Properties
rows.textLatex:
Write short notes on any two
i) Gamma distribution.
ii) Probability generating function of random variables and its applications.
iii) Properties of autocorrelation functions of WSS random processes

rows.topic: Sample Mean Moments & Central Limit Theorem
rows.textLatex: Establish the relations between the expectation and the variance of the sample mean and the corresponding quantities of the population. Also discuss the significance of the central limit theorem.

rows.topic: Bridge Load Normal & CLT Application
rows.textLatex: Civil engineers believe that $W$, the amount of weight (in units of $1,000$ pounds) that a certain span of a bridge can withstand without structural damage resulting, is normally distributed with mean $400$ and standard deviation $40$. Suppose that the weight (again, in units of $1,000$ pounds) of a car is a random variable with mean $3$ and standard deviation $0.3$. How many cars would have to be on the bridge span for the probability of structural damage to exceed $0.1$?

rows.topic: Upper Confidence Interval for Normal Mean
rows.textLatex: Explain the significance of the term '95% upper confidence interval' in connection with estimation of the mean of a normal population with known variance.

rows.topic: Two-Sided and Upper Confidence Intervals for Normal Mean
rows.textLatex:
A signal having value $\mu$ is transmitted from location A and the value received at B is normally distributed with mean $\mu$ and variance $6.25$. If the successive received values are
$6.5, 8.0, 14.5, 9.5, 10.5, 5.0, 7.5, 12.5 \text{ \& } 8.5$,
then determine the $95\%$ confidence interval for $\mu$. Also determine its $99\%$ upper confidence interval.

rows.topic: Hypothesis Testing Definitions & Error Types
rows.textLatex: Define the terms, (i) Simple Hypothesis, (ii) Composite Hypothesis, (iii) Type I error, (iv) Type II error, (v) Critical Region.

rows.topic: Hypothesis Testing for Normal Mean (Known Variance)
rows.textLatex: Suppose it is known that if a signal of value $\mu$ is sent from station A, then the value received at station B is normally distributed with mean $\mu$ and variance $4$. It is suspected that the signal value $\mu = 8$ will be sent today from A. Test this hypothesis if the same signal value is independently sent five times and the average value received at B is $\bar{X} = 9.5$. Consider $5\%$ significance level.

rows.topic: Least Squares Estimators in Simple Linear Regression
rows.textLatex: Derive the expressions for the Least Square Estimators of the Regression Parameters of a simple linear regression model.

rows.topic: Expected Values of Simple Linear Regression Parameters
rows.textLatex: Determine the expected values of Regression Parameters of a simple linear regression model.

rows.topic: Continuity Correction
rows.textLatex: What is "continuity correction"? Explain it with a suitable example.

rows.topic: Chi-Square and t-Distribution of Sample Variance & Mean
rows.textLatex: If $\bar{X}$ is the sample mean and $S^2$ is the sample variance from a normal population with mean $\mu$ and standard deviation $\sigma$, then show that $(n-1)S^2/\sigma^2$ has a chi-square distribution with $(n-1)$ degrees of freedom and $\sqrt{n}(\bar{X} - \mu)/S$ has a $t$-distribution with $(n-1)$ degrees of freedom where $n$ is the sample size.
